Millionaire Bucks's prizes make it a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. Of the prize money still unclaimed, most is in wins under $2,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

Today's free summary of "Millionaire Bucks" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
952.headline: What type of game it is

959.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "LOTERIA®", only a small slice are still unsold. The game is close to selling out, with two of eight top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Every line of LOTERIA®'s prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
959.headline: Tickets sold so far

972.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$8 Million Money Maker" have been sold. The game is past the halfway point of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

If "$8 Million Money Maker" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
972.headline: How far along this game is

975.body:
The prize money on "$1,000,000 Money Rush" leans toward small, frequent prizes. It is spread over eleven prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $1 million. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

Everything above about "$1,000,000 Money Rush" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
975.headline: How this game pays out

976.body:
All the top prizes on "100X The Cash" have been claimed. That lowers the biggest prize from $2 million to $10,000. Two of those are still out there. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

The numbers for "100X The Cash" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
976.headline: Big prize shown, none left

980.body:
The top prize count on "20X The Cash" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has three of eight top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Everything here about "20X The Cash" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through November 20.
980.headline: Top prizes are still left

"50X The Cash" has 119,375 prizes of $10 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $50,000 prize, with one left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If "50X The Cash" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
981.headline: The prize table, line by line

985.body:
The key fact about "MAX-A-MILLION" is how its thirteen prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward many smaller prizes. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

For "MAX-A-MILLION" or any game, being late in a run is not automatically good or bad. The same numbers mean different things near the end of a run.

Everything above about "MAX-A-MILLION" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.

992.body:
The most common win left on "$2 MILLION VAULT" is $20. The second biggest prize left is $100,000, and one of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

If "$2 MILLION VAULT" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
992.headline: A close look at the prizes

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has had no $5,000 top prize claimed for five months. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "$5,000 Triple Play" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.

994.headline: Early stage or late

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" has two of four top prizes left and is well into its run. About two-thirds of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Today's free summary of "$200,000 Triple Play" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
